title: After a 10-year redemption arc, No Man's Sky is coming to the iPhone and iPad
author: Samuel Axon
summary_long: Just over 10 years after its initial release, space exploration and survival crafting game No Man's Sky is making its way to the iPhone and iPad, Apple and developer Hello Games announced today. It will run on devices as far back as the iPhone 11 and the third-generation iPad Air. No Man's Sky might not have the most cutting-edge AAA graphics (though they're still strong, and they've come a long way since launch via updates), but the game's uncommon method of generating galaxies of incomprehensible scale on device consistently for all players from a single-seed happening on a phone is remarkable for those of us who remember phones performing far behind consoles or desktop PCs. id: bigtech:who report on russian lab worker death highlights key uncert:2026-10-12T18:46:43.000Z
title: WHO report on Russian lab worker death highlights "key uncertainty"
author: Beth Mole
summary_long: Over the weekend, the World Health Organization released a disease outbreak report on the events surrounding the death of a Russian infectious disease researcher earlier this month, highlighting that Russia has yet to report a confirmed cause of death. With that "key uncertainty," the United Nations health agency said it remains impossible to assess the risk of the event or whether the public health measures Russia took were adequate to prevent spread of the unknown disease. The WHO reported that, so far, it has seen no evidence of ongoing transmission of the mystery disease. "However, confidence in the assessment remains limited by the absence of a confirmed etiological diagnosis, and the remaining uncertainty regarding the source and mode of exposure," the agency wrote in its report. id: space:nasas spacex crs35 mission to launch health research:2026-10-12T17:45:27.000Z
title: NASA’s SpaceX CRS-35 Mission to Launch Health Research
summary_long: NASA experiments focused on human and plant health and drug-resistant organisms will travel to the International Space Station aboard SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, advancing research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration. This research supports astronaut health during long-duration missions through four investigations from the agency’s Biological and Physical Sciences division, including 3D models of the human brain, a crop disease study, a faster way to assess astronaut health, and an analysis of antibiotic-resistant bacteria aboard the space station. Tiny brain models, big questions A new precision health investigation helps address a key question: What happens to the human brain in space? The experiment sends small, lab-grown models of the human brain to the orbiting laboratory for five weeks. Source: science.nasa.gov. Date: 2026-10-12.
